newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies higher.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while pork belly futures were expected to open 0.250 to 1.000 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Steady to lower cash hog indications and lower wholesale pork prices could weigh on hog futures. However, trading could be choppy and futures may find spillover support from pork belly futures after Tuesday's monthly USDA Cold Storage Report, they said.
Total pork was up, but this had been expected as stocks grew in anticipation of increased exports to Japan, they said.
The latest CME lean hog index fell $0.80 to $83.23 per cwt.

The Cold Storage report was generally viewed as bullish to pork bellies as it showed a decline in stocks during April for only the second time on record. Belly stocks are now below a year ago and should prompt demand in pork belly futures, analysts said.

However, Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town storage report showed a net in-movement near the high end of expectations which could curb gains somewhat in the pork belly pit. But the rate of storings going into approved warehouses was still running below the year-ago pace, they said.
